findings.title: Multi-domain inputs have no consistent output contract
findings.location: §3.1 Four-Stage Flow; §6.2 System Prompt; §6.4 Output Contract; §11.2 PlannerMultiDomainTests
findings.evidence: §3.1 Stage 4 output shows `resolved_terms: [ResolvedTerm, ...]`; §6.2 says `select the ONE row` and returns a single `resolved_term`; §6.4 defines singular `ResolvedTerm : VocabularyResolution`; §11.2 expects `"tap a 6-32 UNC hole in titanium" produces queries across threads AND materials AND manufacturing domains`.
findings.problem: The spec allows one utterance to generate multiple domain queries but only defines a singular resolved-term result in the actual synthesis/output contract.
findings.why_it_matters: This is impossible to implement consistently. A valid multi-domain utterance must either lose terms, invent undocumented batching, or violate the DTO/prompt contract.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide whether a single utterance resolves one term or many. If many, change the synthesizer prompt, JSON schema, DTOs, decoration payload, and tests to return a collection. If one, prohibit multi-domain inputs at the planner/agent boundary and remove conflicting tests/examples.

findings.title: Planner alias fallback references `@utterance`, but planner input does not contain the utterance
findings.location: §5.1 Role; §5.2 Deterministic Grammar Rules (Thread Callouts); §4.4 Output Contract
findings.evidence: §5.1 says the planner `takes a BouncerResult`; §5.2 fallback is `SELECT canonical_id FROM vocab.aliases WHERE alias_text = @utterance`; §4.4 `BouncerResult` has Decision, Reason, CandidateDomains, ParsedIntent, CacheHit, LatencyMs, but no utterance field.
findings.problem: The specified alias-lookup path cannot be executed because the required input is absent from the planner contract.
findings.why_it_matters: Thread resolution falls through to an unimplementable branch for non-grammar matches.
findings.proposed_fix: Add raw and/or normalized utterance text to the planner input contract, or rewrite the fallback to use only fields that actually exist in `BouncerResult`.

findings.title: Synthesis prompt depends on raw utterance that Stage 4 does not pass
findings.evidence: §3.1 Stage 4 input is `ResultSets + BouncerDecision.intent`; §6.2 says the synthesizer receives `(a) a user utterance and parsed intent` and rule 1 checks whether a row `exactly matches the utterance's subject/parameters`.
findings.problem: The Stage 4 contract omits the raw utterance required by the synthesis rules.
findings.why_it_matters: Exact-match and disambiguation behavior cannot be implemented as specified because the synthesizer never receives one of its declared inputs.
findings.proposed_fix: Carry raw/normalized utterance through the pipeline and define it explicitly in the synthesizer request schema.

findings.title: Audit citation persistence is declared mandatory but implemented as fire-and-forget
findings.location: §2 SDR-07-006; §3.2 Latency Budget; §3.3 Failure Modes; §8.2 Decoration Payload Shape
findings.evidence: §2 says `Every resolution records its citation in a decoration payload`; §3.2 says `Decoration write (async) ... Fire-and-forget; not in critical path`; §3.3 lists failure modes but none for decoration-write failure.
findings.problem: The spec guarantees DHF citation recording while choosing a persistence mode that can fail silently with no retry, no surfaced result, and no rollback behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: The core audit/compliance objective can be missed without detection, leaving tool calls executed with no recorded vocabulary citation.
findings.proposed_fix: Make decoration persistence part of the success path, or specify a durable queue/retry/idempotency mechanism plus explicit failure handling when decoration persistence fails.

findings.title: Mandatory demo 2 requires material resolution capability that mandatory scope does not require
findings.evidence: Mandatory scope requires `Query planner with thread grammar rules (§5.2) and fastener grammar rules (§5.4)` and repository methods `GetByCanonicalIdAsync`, `FindByAliasAsync`, `GetThreadAsync`, `GetMaterialAsync`, `GetFastenerAsync`; the same section requires demo 2: `"specify the plate in titanium, medical grade" — vocabulary resolves to `ASTM_F136:Ti_6Al_4V_ELI``.
findings.problem: The mandatory feature list omits the material grammar/search path needed to turn free text into a material canonical ID. `GetMaterialAsync` only fetches after the ID is already known.
findings.why_it_matters: A stated mandatory demo cannot be built from the declared mandatory implementation scope.
findings.proposed_fix: Move material grammar and a material lookup method into mandatory scope, or remove demo 2 from mandatory acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Thread class defaults to `2B` unconditionally when omitted
findings.evidence: For pattern `"<number>-<number> <series> <class>?"`, the spec says `Normalize: ... default class = 2B`.
findings.problem: The parser assigns an internal-thread class even when the utterance could refer to an external thread or a generic thread reference.
findings.why_it_matters: Common inputs with omitted class will be silently misresolved instead of escalated, producing wrong canonical IDs.
findings.proposed_fix: Only default to `2B` when intent explicitly indicates an internal thread/hole/tap. Otherwise keep class unspecified and force ambiguity/disambiguation.

findings.title: Several advertised domains have no repository/query contract
findings.evidence: §1 and §4.2 include domains such as `manufacturing`, `welding`, `drawing_abbrev`, `units`, and `primitives`; §9.1 exposes only thread/material/fastener/gdnt/sw_api/med_anatomy methods and finders.
findings.problem: The closed domain set promises supported categories that have no defined repository surface or domain-specific retrieval path.
findings.why_it_matters: Accepted bouncer outputs for those domains have no specified execution path, creating undefined behavior for valid inputs.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove unsupported domains from v1 scope/prompt/`VocabDomains.All`, or add schema, repository methods, planner rules, and tests for each domain.

findings.title: Security-event logging stores full utterance text with no redaction controls
findings.evidence: `logged at LogLevel.Warning with the full utterance text` and the spec includes medical-device vocabulary in §5.7.
findings.problem: Raw transcripts are written to warning logs for security events without any stated redaction, retention, or tenant-boundary controls.
findings.why_it_matters: Logs become a leakage path for sensitive design or regulated medical content.
findings.proposed_fix: Default to redacted or hashed utterance logging and specify a protected audit sink, access control, and retention policy for any full-text capture.

findings.title: Confidence configuration is underspecified relative to the decision table
findings.evidence: §6.3 says `≥ 0.85` accept, `0.70 – 0.85` accept with low-confidence logging, `0.50 – 0.70` ambiguity; §13 exposes `confidenceFloorForResolution: 0.70` and `ambiguityThreshold: 0.85`.
findings.problem: The spec never defines the exact algorithm that uses these two config values, so multiple incompatible implementations are plausible.
findings.why_it_matters: Threshold behavior can drift across code, tests, and configuration because the mapping from config to behavior is not explicit.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one deterministic threshold algorithm in pseudocode and bind each configuration field to a single branch of that algorithm, or collapse to one source-of-truth setting.

findings.title: Build-breaking tests depend on live LLM latency and behavior
findings.evidence: `BouncerAcceptRejectTests` requires model outputs to match seeded classifications; `BouncerLatencyTests` says p95 under 600ms and `fails the build if exceeded on CI`; `PipelineLatencyTests` enforces full-pipeline p95 under 1.2s.
findings.problem: The build is coupled to external-provider latency and nondeterministic model behavior, which the codebase cannot control.
findings.why_it_matters: CI can fail for network/provider drift rather than regressions, reducing signal and blocking delivery unpredictably.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep build-breaking tests on mocks/recorded fixtures and move live-model latency/behavior checks to scheduled canaries or non-blocking release gates.

top_3_must_fix: Define whether one utterance resolves one term or many, and align planner/synthesis/DTOs/tests to that decision.
Propagate raw utterance through planner and synthesis inputs; current alias and exact-match rules require data the contracts do not carry.
Make DHF decoration persistence reliable or explicitly fail/retry when citation logging cannot be written.
